newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Incentive sells half ABB stake.
newsitem.headline: Incentive sells half ABB stake.

text.p: Swedish Investment and medical technology group Incentive said on Wednesday it had sold half its stake in ABB AB for 12.4 billion crowns to institutions and investment group Investor.
Incentive said in a statement the sale will generate a 9.9 billion crown capital gain, or about 8.5 billion crowns after tax.
"Incentive continues to pursue its rapid restructuring and this divestment represents an important step in this process," Incentive's chief executive Mikael Lilius said in the statement.
"It will serve to focus the group and significantly reduces our debt."

Incentive said it had sold 110 million series A shares in ABB AB -- the Swedish parent company of Swiss-Swedish engineer ABB -- corresponding to 11.7 percent of the capital and 15.8 percent of the votes.
"Of these shares, 54.5 million shares have been sold to Morgan Stanley Dean Witter for resale to institutional investors in Sweden and internationally," Incentive said in a statement.
"The remaining 55.6 million shares have been sold to Investor AB."
Morgan Stanley paid six billion crowns for its stake which corresponded to 5.8 percent of capital and 7.8 percent of votes.
Investor will pay Wednesday's closing market price of 114.5 crowns a share, or 6.4 billion crowns, for shares corresponding to 5.9 percent of the capital and eight percent of the votes.
"The proceeds for the shares sold to Investor will be paid on January 30, 1998, when the shares are transferred," Incentive said. "Until this date interest will be paid on the agreed purchase price."

After the transaction, Investor will hold 6.4 percent of the capital and 8.6 percent of votes in ABB AB while Incentive will own about 118 million series A shares or 12.6 percent of the capital and 16.9 percent of the votes.
"Incentive has committed to Morgan Stanley Dean Witter not to make any further sales of ABB shares through March 1, 1998," the company said.
"The timing and size of the sale of the ABB shares coincides with our acquisition of Vivra, the second largest dialysis provider in the U.S.," Lilius said.
Incentive's tender offer for Vivra shares closed earlier this week with 97 percent of Vivra's shareholders accepting the offer.
"We can now fully integrate Vivra into our (medical technology unit) Gambro AB, thereby strengthening our leading global position in renal care and renal products," Lilius said.
Investor chief executive Claes Dahlback said the group wanted continued ownership of ABB while Incentive, in which Investor holds a major stake, restructured.
"We have already stated that medical technology is a promising area and this reorientation of Incentive is therefore in line with our strategy," Dahlback said.
